newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Tranz Rail raises first quarter profit.
newsitem.headline: Tranz Rail raises first quarter profit.

text.p: Rail and ferry operator Tranz Rail Holdings Ltd said on Friday it increased first quarter net profit to NZ$9.4 million from $5.8 million in the previous corresponding period.
It said the increase reflected lower interest costs and increased traffic levels.
Total revenue for quarter ended September 30 was NZ$133.9 million, up three percent.
Revenue rose 1.9 percent for freight, 9.4 percent for ferry operations between the North and South Islands and 5.1 percent for rail passengers, while other revenue declined slightly.

Total operating costs were up 3.3 percent at NZ$115.9 million, while labour costs rose $1.6 million or 3.2 percent. This reflected increased traffic, wage rate increases on a year to year basis and higher provisions for staff incentive plans.
Materials costs fell 27.5 percent through use of reusable materials and falling maintenance expenditure as a consequence of capital improvements to rolling stock and track infrastructure.

Operating profit rose 1.1 percent to NZ$18 million, while net interest expense and financing costs amortisation fell to $3.9 million from $8.8 million. This reflected repayment of long-term debt following the company's global initial public offering in June 1996.
Tax rose to NZ$4.7 million from $3.2 million.
Tranz Rail's major shareholders are Wisconsin Central Transportation Corp; U.S. private equity firm Berkshire Partners; Pacific Rail, a Fay Richwhite and Co subsidiary; and David Lloyd Investments.
